ratings_why.fun: Watching every buff land twice on a rested board, then a Wake domino or a Dragon flood, is a satisfying grow-and-cash-in arc; the counter math on every unit holds it back from more.
ratings_why.distinct: Rest as a doubler that prices stillness and lifts other tribes' buffs is fresh for an auto-battler, though the Wake chain plays like a familiar death-trigger chain.

verdict_why: The cards now say permanently, the Wake order and timing are written, and what's left is UI and wording polish, not rules that fail.

points.text: Readability rests on the UI: every unit needs its Rest visible and every buff needs its doubled result previewed, or players will misjudge every buffer they buy.
Old Polh says "your units" while Rest and Vespers Bat say "you own", which includes hand. Use the same words so players know whether rested units in hand get the +1/+1.
The Wake build needs Vespers Bat earlier in reading order than Lamplighter and Old Polh, which no card says. A small slot-order cue on the board would make this puzzle readable.
Dragon of the Springs and the Robber-Knight both empty Rest at Start of Combat, so whichever fires first leaves the other nothing. Worth a line on both cards or a preview, since it reads as a trap.

The fantasy carries in play: holding still is the olm's patience, the Dragon is the flood bringing the deep up, Parkelj is the one who's awake, Ribica's every-12th is the clutch. Keep these as the tribe settles.

standouts.why: Floods bringing the deep to the surface, as one clear Start of Combat cash-in of a whole game's stillness.
The awake black olm who eats everyone's sleep: the anti-synergy reads at a glance and tells his story.
One short line that flips the tribe to hoarding forever and says so on the card.

weakest.why: Dormouse Pilgrim is plain gold-for-stillness with little of the tribe's own mechanic in it.
Pool Olmling's three clauses (lose Rest when a neighbour is played, Wake, regain Rest) are a lot to read on a Tier 1 seed.
Gift-Shop Friar's per-4-Rest sale math is fiddly for a small economy payoff.

flags.note: Doubling every permanent gain without spending Rest stacks with Cloister Keeper and other tribes' growth; worth the owner's eye with percentage growth.
Copies of your biggest Sleeper can triple into a golden that keeps all buffs; a jackpot that could run away.
"Your units with Rest" may or may not include rested units in hand.
